content.thinking:
I'm going to fix the root cause here: rather than naming the revision, I'll describe each usage according to its own row. The reconciliation check compares the field against the sum, which is fine. The statements read it and divide by it.

I also want to revisit chain step 4, where I said that code using it still reads the stored field instead of deriving it. That may have the same problem, so I'll refine it too.

action_items.item: Export the accounts and run Code-Fix's repair script against them (scripts/repair_monthly_totals.py), first as a dry run and then with --apply, and load the corrected accounts back. Do this once a revision that maintains the month total is running, and before the month rolls over.
Run the spend-integrity check that compares stored monthly totals with the purchases far more often than it runs now.

Add a test that runs for every change to the purchase ledger. It should record purchases through each write path (record_purchase, record_purchase_deriving_the_month and record_a_purchase both ways) and assert that reconcile_monthly_totals reports nothing for the result.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' stored monthly spend totals no longer matched the purchases behind them: each affected total came out short of what the shopper had bought this month.

Purchases recorded on the running code were added to the account and to the lifetime total, but the stored this-month total was left where it was. The reconciliation check compares that stored figure with the sum of the in-month purchases, so it found the stored figure short.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 4c810f2 at {P1.1}: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, which is after the later deploy at {P2.1}.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider's history showed {T14.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus in the window before the onset.

causal_chain.step: Revision 26f1d7e, deployed at {P2.1}, removed the update to total_this_month_cents from record_purchase. As of {T11.1}, all {T11.2} replicas were running that revision.

The change stopped keeping the month total on the reasoning that it could be derived from the history, but it left the stored field in place, and the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation check all still read that stored field.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change to the shop stopped updating each shopper's saved running total for the current month when a purchase was recorded, but the shop's statements and checks still read that saved total, so it fell further behind what shoppers had actually bought.

contributing_factors.factor: The only thing that found the drift was the spend-integrity check, which runs once every {A5} days. No more frequent check was seen comparing stored monthly totals with the purchases behind them.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran more often would have caught the wrong totals soon after the deploy, so far fewer totals would have been written wrong before anyone knew.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Before the change was deployed, no check was seen that records purchases through the ledger's write paths and confirms the stored monthly total still matches the purchases.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a check would have failed on a change that stopped moving the month total, and the change would have been held back before it reached production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the deployment's diff, which showed the month-total update removed from record_purchase.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone else before the onset, which ruled out a flag change.
Argus declined to roll back on its own, because nothing would show inside its wait whether the rollback worked. It left the rollback to a person as a recommendation instead.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a draft pull request, #554, along with a one-off repair script for the totals already written wrong.

went_wrong: The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it, so the rollback Argus recommended waited on a person noticing it.

input.root_cause: The change removed the line in record_purchase that added each in-month purchase's price to the account's stored total_this_month_cents, on the reasoning that the month could be derived from the purchase history, yet left the stored field in place. The monthly statement still reads that field as the month total and divides it by the number of purchases to get the mean, the spend summary divides it by the number of this month's purchases, and the reconciliation check compares it with the sum of this month's purchase prices. So every purchase recorded afterwards left the stored figure further behind the purchases.
input.still_at_risk: Every purchase recorded through either write path on the running revision could keep leaving shoppers' stored monthly totals short, and the totals already written wrong stay wrong in the monthly statements and spend figures that read them until someone rewrites them.
input.symptom: Shoppers' monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
